newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast gasolines firm on supply concerns.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast gasolines firm on supply concerns.

text.p: U.S. West Coast gasoline prices firmed Friday, continuing the week's strong gains on fears of diminished gasoline supply, traders said.
The union representing Unocal's oil refinery workers has decided to terminate its contract by late Monday, setting up the possibility of strikes at four California plants.
"It's significant, especially with the position the West Coast is in right now," one trader said, noting supplies were down 5.3 million barrels from last year's levels.
The four Unocal refineries process 250,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) of crude and make 20 percent of California's gasoline.
Gasoline also found strength because of prolonged maintenance at Exxon, Mobil, and Unocal plants, which are expected to return next week.
Deals for CARB grade unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles were done at 84.25 cents for March, and 81.50 cents for April.
Bids for conventional unleaded gasoline in Los Angeles rose two cents to 80 cents a gallon, while buyers valued CARB-grade material two cents higher at 83 cents.
Offers for San Francisco conventional rose three cents to 81 cents.
